I finally fixed a bug with certain borders not appearing. I really should have done this sooner, but I was hamstrung by perfectionism. I'll say a few words about that, but first, the fix:

~~~ .light:not(#foo) #container input[type="text"], .light:not(#foo) #container textarea { border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.2) !important; }

.dark:not(#foo) #container input[type="text"], .dark:not(#foo) #container textarea { border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.15) !important; } ~~~

Simply add the above code after Cashmere in your theme's custom stylesheet and change the colours if necessary (it's probably not).

This snippet fixes all versions of Cashmere and should not adversely affect any custom modifications you've made.

I'll add this code to the releases in the Cashmere repo later today. Done.

----

Now, on why it took me so long to fix this relatively simple problem...

The problem of borders not appearing on certain text input elements [started about six months ago](https://voat.co/v/Cashmere/comments/484028). I still don't know exactly what caused it, but I assume the Voat stylesheet changed in some way. In any case, it's pretty terrible UI to not have borders showing where the inputs are.

My thought process went something like this:

> This issue is partly caused by the ham-fisted way Cashmere manages CSS specificity. I understand specificity much better now than when I started, so I can refactor Cashmere to solve not only the border issue, but prevent future headaches. It will all be dealt with in the next release.

The problem, of course, is there has not been another release since then.

Last night I was watching [a talk by Harry Roberts](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8adsZeMQjGQ) where he says:

> Pragmatism trumps perfection. Something hacky that works today is better than something perfect that might work next week.

I was immediately reminded of the border issue and my perfect solution that never materialized. Then I spent about 20 minutes writing a hacky fix that works today.

In my head, I had equated "I should fix the borders" with "I should refactor everything". Big mistake. The job of fixing the borders should have been done immediately and imperfectly. I still have the option of correcting the underlying specificity issue in the future. Lesson learned.
